doc: Generated by tools/casestudy.py from whitepaper.md §11 and Appendix A, the law IR maps_to, spec/ledger/maps_to.json, the result records, the replay reports and results/M2/hypotheses.json. Do not edit. The coverage rule is preregistered in the docstring of tests_m2/test_casestudy.py (I4 prereg 15ecf46); the tool's docstring restates it. Counts are derived data, not predictions. 'full' means the obstruction was observed on every replay side, whatever the side's provenance; full_with_finding lists the full obstructions with a law in the provisional finding bin.

N1.title: O15: η₂ wrote CSR only at the last committed index. Suppose: at migration, LFI = a < LCI = b; and the owner later reverts into (a, b]. Then every commit fails the CSR equality check, and remains blocked until an upgrade. The obstruction is latent and historical, and was missed because the manual analysis modeled only the current version.

N2.title: O12: Cancelling a challenge leaves the +W extensions it applied to other batches. An intent contract (§5.9) can bound this as designed behaviour.

N3.title: O25: Under the BVH pin, the content of the recommitted batch is fixed by the original submitter S₁, while the bond at risk is the recommitter S₂'s. A rational S₂ therefore refuses to recommit unprovable content, which turns slashing into a liveness deterrent.

N4.title: O14: Legacy committers cannot prove their own in-flight batches after the cutover. If no prover in the new registry acts within W, a possibly valid batch is reverted.

law_notes.L_par_hdr_ssvh: Bears on D1: the Solidity commit path always writes sequencerSetVerifyHash = 0, while Go BatchHeaderV1.Bytes encodes the field, and the pinned Go legacy-replay path can produce a non-zero one (common/batch/batch_cache.go:1447-1472). So D1's 'Solidity ≡ Go except byte 0' holds only under ssvh = 0, the premise L_par_hdr_v0 and L_par_hdr_v1 carry. Mapped to D1, this REFUTED law makes D1 partial under the coverage rule.
law_notes.L_par_hdr_v2: Reproduces O2 against Go's BatchHeaderV1.Bytes, which hard-codes byte 0 = 1. At the pinned commit the Go batch producer does build version-2 headers, by patching byte 0 of BatchHeaderV1.Bytes() and storing the aggregate at [57:89] (common/batch/batch_cache.go:1727-1731), so O2's 'no v2 encoder' clause no longer holds there; the law's comparison is with the v1 encoder only.
law_notes.L_rt_go_v0: Go getters recover every field of the header Solidity commits: the decoding half of D1.
law_notes.L_rt_go_v2: As L_rt_go_v0, version 2 (D1 names v0/v1 layouts; v2 reuses the v1 wire format).
